papers.title: A counterexample on the main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles
papers.abstract: The main flatness conjecture for $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundles predicts the existence of a unique strongly positive flat compatible Hermitian metric for every $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$-Fock bundle. We use cyclic Higgs bundles to disprove this conjecture for every rank $n \geq 3.$

papers.title: Entropy-degree rigidity for non-collapsed $RCD$ spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the entropy-degree theorem for continuous maps from a closed orientable non-collapsed $RCD(K,N)$ space $X$ to a closed negatively curved locally symmetric $N$-manifold $Y$, with $N \geq 3$. In the equality case, under a fundamental group index condition, we show the space is isometric to a smooth locally symmetric Riemannian manifold, and the map is homotopic to a Riemannian covering.

papers.title: A Chord-Arc Estimate for Graphical Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove an interior chord-arc estimate for graphical hypersurfaces without an a priori gradient bound, which is not restricted to balls on the scale of their curvature. As a main application we derive an in-radius lower bound depending on the curvature which then also implies Heinz-type estimates for minimal graphs and uniform area bounds for graphical hypersurfaces.

papers.title: Liouville type results for super-$p$-biharmonic immersions and $p$-biharmonic submanifolds
papers.abstract: We introduce a weak notion of $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion into Euclidean space, formulated through a divergence inequality for the mean curvature vector. This class naturally extends the $\varepsilon$-superbiharmonic immersions previously introduced by the third author while remaining well-defined for all $p>1$, including the singular range $1<p<2$. We prove a Liouville-type rigidity theorem showing that every proper $\varepsilon$-super-$p$-biharmonic immersion is minimal provided \[ \liminf_{r\to\infty} \frac1{r^{2}} \int_{f^{-1}(B_r)} |\vec{H}| ^{q}\,d\mu=0 \] for some $q>p-\varepsilon$. This extends the corresponding superbiharmonic rigidity theorem to the $p$-biharmonic setting under a natural growth hypothesis. We also establish a minimality theorem for complete $p$-biharmonic immersions into Riemannian manifolds of non-positive sectional curvature under a polynomial growth assumption on the mean curvature. More precisely, if \[ \int_{B_r(x_0)} | \vec{H} | ^{\,q}\,d\mu = O(r^d) \] for some $q\ge0$ and $d>0$, then the immersion is minimal. For $q=0$ this recovers the polynomial volume-growth theorem of Cao--Luo \cite{CL16}, while for $q>0$ it provides a polynomial-growth analogue of Han's $L^q$-integrability rigidity theorem \cite{H15}.

papers.title: Prescribed inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature flow on finite trees
papers.abstract: We characterize the image of the inverse-weight Lin-Lu-Yau curvature map on finite edge-weighted trees. We prove that the prescribed curvature flow converges if and only if the target curvature is attainable, and that the convergence is exponential whenever it occurs. The key ingredient in the proof is a formulation of the prescribed curvature flow as the gradient flow of a convex functional.

papers.title: Polynomial approximations to Calabi--Yau metrics on quartic K3 surfaces and quintic threefolds
papers.abstract: On the Fermat quartic K3 surface and the Fermat quintic threefold, we construct K\"ahler metrics from explicit rational polynomial potentials and bound their differences from the Ricci-flat metrics in integral tensor norms. For specified compact families of smooth quartic and quintic hypersurfaces near the Fermat hypersurfaces, we give a terminating algorithm that constructs polynomial K\"ahler metrics with prescribed pointwise bounds on their differences from the Ricci-flat metrics and on their Ricci forms. The resulting metrics converge to the Ricci-flat metrics in every $C^r$ norm, uniformly in the parameter.

papers.title: Classification of G-g.o. metrics on compact homogeneous spaces G/H with G simple
papers.abstract: We classify the $G$-g.o. metrics on compact homogeneous spaces $G/H$, where $G$ is a compact connected simple Lie group and $H$ is an arbitrary closed subgroup. We give the complete list of nonnormal metrics, including their parameter conditions and the possible mixing between equivalent isotropy summands. The proof uses rigidity criteria for arbitrary cometric operators, reductions through centralizers, and the stabilizers of the relevant representations. For every fixed pair $(G,H)$, the space spanned by the $G$-g.o. cometrics has dimension at most three, and we determine the equality cases. We also compare the classification with the compact weakly symmetric pairs and explain why the choice of the transitive group is essential.

papers.title: Harmonic functions and the topology of 3-manifolds under nonnegative scalar curvature
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish and recover some results about noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature and some topological assumptions. Firstly, we apply the work in Oronzio \cite{Oro1,Oro2} to obtain a nonexistence result of the harmonic function. Secondly, we use the argument in Yan-Zhu \cite{YZ} to establish a rigidity result, which states that such manifold is isometric to the warped product of a flat tours and a half line. Finally, we recover a topological result in Yan-Zhu \cite{YZ} via a different argument.

papers.title: Hyperbolicity Notions on Complete Non-Compact Complex Manifolds
papers.abstract: Gromov's K\"ahler hyperbolicity, extended by McMullen to complete manifolds of finite volume and bounded geometry, has non-K\"ahler analogues (balanced, SKT, Gauduchon and divisorial hyperbolicity) that have so far been studied only on compact manifolds. We define these notions for complete Hermitian manifolds and prove the following. A manifold carrying a balanced metric and a Hermitian metric with bounded $(\partial+\bar\partial)$-potentials satisfies a Cheeger inequality, so its fundamental group is non-amenable in the compact case. K\"ahler and SKT hyperbolic manifolds are Brody hyperbolic, and balanced and Gauduchon hyperbolic manifolds are divisorially hyperbolic, without any compactness assumption. Products give complete non-compact non-K\"ahler examples. A non-compact surface may be divisorially hyperbolic without being Brody hyperbolic. Finally, no functorial pseudo-distance characterises divisorial hyperbolicity.}

papers.title: Dirac eigenvalue comparison
papers.abstract: We study how curvature bounds control the Dirac eigenvalues of closed spin manifolds, comparing the positive and negative eigenvalues separately. Within a fixed conformal class and spin structure, pointwise ordering of scalar curvature relative to a metric of negative scalar curvature implies comparison at every nonzero index. On the two-sphere, a holomorphic ladder on the half-canonical bundle proves the corresponding comparison in both directions under a Gaussian curvature bound. On surfaces of higher genus, the same bundle identities propagate comparison from the scalar and spinor levels to higher canonical powers. In the round conformal class on the higher dimensional sphere, a prescribed scalar curvature bound yields an upper bound in absolute value for the first $2^{[n/2]}$ Dirac eigenvalues. When the conformal class varies, we can show that the corresponding comparisons on hyperbolic surfaces and odd-dimensional spheres no longer hold; while on even-dimensional spheres, the first gap and all sufficiently high-index eigenvalues of either sign satisfy a one-direction comparison.

papers.title: A note on equivariant twisted holomorphic analytic torsion
papers.abstract: In this note, we introduce an equivariant version of twisted holomorphic analytic torsion for the twisted Dolbeault complex on a complex manifold equipped with an action of a compact Lie group. Our construction is motivated by Ray and Singer's holomorphic analytic torsion, by the equivariant analytic torsion developed for elliptic complexes with group actions, notably in the work of Donnelly and later in the holomorphic setting by Bismut, and by Mathai and Wu's twisted analytic torsion for the twisted de Rham complex. Using pseudodifferential operators and the equivariant noncommutative residue, we define the equivariant twisted holomorphic analytic torsion. We also state its variation formulas under changes of the metric and of the twisting element, and present its functorial properties.

papers.title: Weighted minimal surfaces in H2 x R invariant under hyperbolic translations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR, namely, surfaces that arise as critical points of a weighted area functional, where the corresponding weight depends only on the height function associated with the second factor R. We refer to these surfaces as {\phi}-minimal surfaces. For a class of increasing and concave weight potential functions {\phi}, we focus our attention on height-weighted minimal surfaces that are invariant under isometries of H2xR that act trivially on R and act by hyperbolic translations in H2. Through a detailed analysis of the corresponding three-dimensional system of ordinary differential equations, we present families of entire graphs, graphs over half-spaces of H2 that are asymptotic to vertical planes, winglike surfaces, and surfaces whose height function has no minimum. These families show that the hyperbolic-invariant setting is considerably richer than the rotational and parabolic settings. For the class of potential functions {\phi} we consider, they also allow us to classify all weighted minimal surfaces in H2xR that are invariant under hyperbolic translations.

papers.title: Determinant Identities and Branch Selection in the Stationary Multi-Horizon Balance Problem
papers.abstract: We study the Hennig-Neugebauer family of stationary and axisymmetric vacuum multi-horizon candidates. The regularity conditions on the symmetry axis lead to quadratic determinant relations which leave an apparent ambiguity between two sign branches. Under explicit non-degeneracy assumptions, we prove that one of these branches is impossible. This branch selection yields a system of explicit determinant equations characterizing equilibrium within the family.

papers.title: HKT-Einstein metrics on circle bundles
papers.abstract: We consider a construction of hyper-Hermitian structures on total spaces of circle bundles over 3-quasi-Sasakian manifolds. We study the HKT-Einstein equation in this setting, proving that a large family of non-homogeneous hyper-complex manifolds admit compatible HKT-Einstein metrics with positive Einstein factor. We also show that the hyper-Hermitian structures on such circle bundles are quaternionic balanced or quaternionic Gauduchon if and only if they are HKT. Finally, the HKT-Einstein condition is investigated under the twist construction.

papers.title: Entropic Ricci bounds at conic singularities and boundaries
papers.abstract: We study synthetic Ricci bounds and related rigidity phenomena in conic and boundary neighborhoods through the behavior of entropy along optimal transports. For cones over manifolds, we show that two-sided entropic Ricci bounds at the vertex force the fiber to have constant sectional curvature 1, while non-trivial quotient singularities, such as Euclidean cones over spherical space forms, remain admissible. An analogous rigidity holds for Riemannian manifolds with conic singularities. We also give a local characterization of boundary convexity in terms of entropic lower Ricci bounds, based on a direct optimal transport argument.

papers.title: Poisson and Jacobi structures on quadratic Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We study Poisson and Jacobi structures compatible with quadratic structures on finite-dimensional Lie algebras, mostly over fields of characteristic zero. Building on the theory of generalized double extensions, we give necessary and sufficient reconstruction criteria for the skew operators preserving a marked isotropic ideal, allowing degenerate operators, a nonabelian quadratic quotient, and the full generalized extension data. Recalling the characterization of quadratic Poisson structures in terms of skew-symmetric solutions of the classical Yang--Baxter equation, we combine the ambient bracket reconstruction of Kostant and Meyer with prescribed symplectic leaf data to reconstruct Poisson structures whose characteristic subalgebra is nondegenerate for the quadratic form. We express the standard algebraic Jacobi equations through the invariant form and obtain analogous reconstruction results for nondegenerate characteristic subalgebras. Particular attention is given to the contact and locally conformally symplectic cases. A common cochain framework identifies the remaining scalar obstruction in third cohomology in the Poisson case and in the Jacobi branch whose Euler element belongs to the marked ideal, with coefficients in a one dimensional module in the latter case. Our reconstruction results yield systematic procedures for constructing quadratic Poisson structures in dimension $n+2k$ from those in dimension $n$, and recover the earlier quadratic symplectic extension formulas when the Poisson operator is invertible. Explicit examples illustrate the applicability of the theory, including oscillator algebras, the five-dimensional Lie algebra $A_{5,3}$, and Poisson structures associated with the curvature tensor of a bi-invariant metric.

papers.title: Generic equivariant simplicity of the spectrum of Laplace-type operators with finite symmetry
papers.abstract: We prove that for generic elements in three natural families of Laplace-type differential operators on smooth manifolds, which are equivariant with respect to a finite symmetry group, all the eigenspaces are irreducible representations. In other words, the spectrum of these operators is generically equivariantly simple. The three families of operators with symmetry are Schr\"odinger operators parametrized by the potential, going back to the work of Wigner, Laplace-Beltrami operators parametrized by invariant Riemannian metrics and conformal Laplacians parametrized by invariant metrics in a given conformal class. The latter two results extend prior work of Zelditch for certain free group actions and resolve, for finite group actions, a well-known open question raised by Guillemin and Yau. Our approach stems from methods developed by Wendl and Doan-Walpuski to address equivariant transversality in symplectic topology.

papers.title: Entire boosted hypersurfaces of vanishing mean curvature in Schwarzschild spacetime
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of entire maximal hypersurfaces, asymptotic to suitable coordinate-dependent boosts in the two asymptotically flat ends of maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime. As a corollary, this generates a foliation of maximal hypersurfaces in exterior Schwarzschild, which corresponds to a geometric choice of time function associated with any boost parameter. As a crucial step in the proof, we introduce a novel rotationally symmetric time function in maximally extended Schwarzschild, which is Cauchy and has properties of independent interest.

papers.title: Addendum to "Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds"
papers.abstract: In the paper ``Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds'', the same authors introduced a geometric object called Pontryagin-type $C^0$-Finsler structures, which includes Finsler structures on a smooth manifold $M$. Such a structure is defined locally by a control system of $C^1$ unit vector fields on an open subset $U$ of $M$, such that Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) is applicable. As a result of PMP, we obtain the extended geodesic field $\mathcal{E}$, which is a multivalued vector field on the slit cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}U\backslash 0 = \{(x,\alpha): x\in U, \alpha \in T^{\ast}_x U\}$, such that every minimizing path $x(t)$ on $(U,F)$ is an extremal (projection of a Pontryagin extremal $(x(t),\alpha(t))$). Some time after its introduction, its use and external comments, it is useful to provide remarks that clarify the applicability and limitations of this theory. In addition, we point out two errors contained in that work which, although discernible from the context, we believe should be pointed out. Finally, we prove some cases where the property that a minimizing path is the projection of a Pontryagin extremal can be extended beyond a coordinate system, sometimes to $M$. We also work on the problem of determining when $\mathcal{E}$ does not depend on the control system chosen to represent $F$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies these two properties globally for left-invariant $C^0$-Finsler structures on Lie groups, and for $C^1$-Finsler structures (without the condition of strong convexity).

papers.title: Holomorphic Sectional Curvature of Flag Manifolds via Kähler Reduction
papers.abstract: We give an alternative proof of Li and Petersen's theorem that every invariant K\"ahler metric on a compact generalized flag manifold has positive holomorphic sectional curvature. For a unitary partial flag manifold, we realize the given metric by K\"ahler reduction of a Hermitian vector space. The defining equations place the level set on a sphere of radius \varrho, where the radial component of its second fundamental form gives the explicit lower bound 4/\varrho2 through the quotient curvature formula. Finally, we use a holomorphic isometric totally geodesic embedding to transfer the bound to generalized flag manifolds of every Lie type.

papers.title: Rigidity of compact quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary and low-dimensional focal sets
authors: Matheus Andrade Ribeiro de Moura Horácio
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate nontrivial compact m-quasi-Einstein manifolds with boundary, m > 1 and constant scalar curvature. We first prove that such a manifold is rigid whenever the set of critical points of its potential function is totally geodesic, which extends to quasi-Einstein manifolds a theorem of Li, Li, Ou, Qu, Wu and Zhou for shrinking Ricci solitons. Then, we prove that, in every dimension, this set is totally geodesic whenever it has dimension two or three, so that the manifold is rigid in this case. The proof is based on a Bochner identity for the covariant derivative of the Ricci tensor at the points of this set. In particular, every such manifold of dimension five is rigid. Finally, we obtain rigidity in arbitrary dimension under an integral Weyl pinching condition when the set of critical points has dimension four.

papers.title: Invariant complex Finsler metrics on reductive complex homogeneous spaces
papers.abstract: Let $(M=G/H,J)$ be a reductive complex homogeneous space and $F$ be a $G$-invariant strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metric on $M$. Using the adapted $(1,0)$-frame field obtained by parallel transformation with respect to the canonical connection on $M$, we obtain the necessary and sufficient condition for $F$ to be a K\"ahler-Finsler metric (resp. weakly K\"ahler-Finsler metric) in terms of Lie-bracket. The curvature tensor of the complex Rund connection associated to $F$ is then decomposed into an algebraic part and a derivative part, yielding explicit formulas for the holomorphic bisectional curvature and holomorphic sectional curvature of $F$, respectively. As an application, we give a Lie-theoretic proof of the rigidity theorem: every $G$-invariant strongly pseudoconvex complex Finsler metric on a complex symmetric manifold $M=G/H$ is necessarily a K\"ahler--Berwald metric.

papers.title: Hessian sectional curvatures of conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds
papers.abstract: Conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds generalize Hessian manifolds. Shima introduced Hessian sectional curvature in 1995 as an invariant for studying Hessian structures. We extend this invariant to conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds and study related curvature conditions and invariants. Our main results are as follows. For connected Hessian manifolds of dimension at least two, we characterize constant Hessian sectional curvature (CHC) by pointwise orthogonal invariance. We call conjugate symmetric statistical manifolds satisfying this invariance condition weakly CHC. We classify connected weakly CHC statistical manifolds of dimension at least two whose cubic forms are parallel with respect to the Levi-Civita connection. This classification characterizes the non-Hessian statistical structures induced on the classical hyperbolic affine spheres $xyz=c>0$ in the positive octant. We also introduce principal Hessian curvatures and show that they form a complete invariant for left-invariant Hessian structures on $\mathbb{R}^n$ up to statistical isomorphism.

papers.title: Kobayashi distance to submanifolds in a Riemannian manifold
papers.abstract: We prove that totally geodesic hypersurfaces are at infinite Kobayashi distance in a Kobayashi hyperbolic Riemannian manifold. To do this, we prove a Schwarz lemma on minimal maps with a uniform control on their Laplacians. Finally we give a full characterisation of submanifolds at infinite distance on spaces of constant sectional curvature in dimension at least 4.

papers.title: On compact homogeneous Locally conformal symplectic manifolds
papers.abstract: A locally conformally symplectic (LCS) structure on a manifold $M$ is a pair $(\eta,\omega)$ consisting of a closed $1$-form $\eta$ called Lee form and a nondegenerate $2$-form $\omega$ satisfying \[ d\omega=\eta\wedge\omega. \] We classify compact connected homogeneous LCS manifolds with nonzero Lee form. To this end, we construct three explicit families of pairs $(G,K)$, where $G$ is a connected simply connected Lie group and $K$ is a closed subgroup such that $G/K$ is compact, the $G$-action is almost effective, and $G/K$ admits a $G$-invariant LCS structure. We show that every compact connected homogeneous LCS manifold with nonzero Lee form arises from one of these families. Moreover, each such manifold is LCS-isomorphic to a product $(S/H_d)\times S^1$, where $S$ is a compact connected simply connected semisimple Lie group and $S/H_d$ carries an $S$-invariant contact form $\alpha$. Under this identification, the LCS structure is given by \[ \eta=\pi_2^*\xi,\qquad \omega=d(\pi_1^*\alpha)+\pi_1^*\alpha\wedge\eta, \] where $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ are the projections onto the two factors and $\xi$ is a nowhere-vanishing $1$-form on $S^1$. This description also yields topological consequences for compact homogeneous LCS manifolds. In particular, none of these compact homogeneous LCS manifolds admits a symplectic structure, even without any invariance assumption. As a consequence, we show that in dimension four the underlying manifolds are precisely $L(d,1)\times S^1$, where $L(d,1)$ is a three-dimensional lens space. In dimension eight, we obtain families arising from seven-dimensional lens spaces and Aloff--Wallach spaces, including infinitely many distinct topological types.

papers.title: Complete critical metrics for the quadratic scalar curvature functional: examples and rigidity
papers.abstract: We study complete critical metrics for the quadratic scalar curvature functional \[ g\mapsto\int_M S_g^2\,\dv_g, \] with criticality understood under compactly supported variations, focusing on rigidity phenomena and nontrivial examples. In dimension three, we prove that every complete critical metric is scalar-flat, without any additional assumption. In dimension four, we construct complete non-Einstein critical metrics with bounded, nonconstant negative scalar curvature. In every dimension $n\geq5$, we show that either $S_g\equiv 0$ or $S_g<0$ everywhere, and a new argument proves scalar-flatness whenever $S_g \in L^p$ for some $0<p\leq P_n$, where $P_n>2$ is an explicit threshold. Moreover, we construct complete critical metrics with bounded, negative scalar curvature, decaying to zero at infinity. These examples establish the optimality of our rigidity threshold $P_n$ in dimension six and in every dimension $n\geq10$. To the best of our knowledge, these are the first complete critical metrics for this functional that are neither scalar-flat nor Einstein.

papers.title: Classification and Geometry of Loxodromic Curves on Surfaces of Revolution in Three-Dimensional Euclidean Space
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the global geometry of loxodromes and loxodromic curves on surfaces of revolution in $\mathbb{R}^3$. A loxodrome is a regular curve avoiding the poles and making a constant directed angle with the meridians. To allow curves to reach or pass through poles, we introduce loxodromic curves, whose pole-free interior portions are loxodromes. The directed azimuths of these portions agree modulo $\pi$. We classify surfaces of revolution into four types based on the number of poles and whether the profile curve is closed: cylinder-like, torus-like, paraboloid-like, and sphere-like. For cylinder-like surfaces, every maximal loxodromic curve other than a parallel is non-self-intersecting. For torus-like surfaces, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves are closed or dense according to the rationality of their rotation numbers. For paraboloid-like and sphere-like surfaces, only maximal meridians can pass smoothly through poles, while nonmeridional, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves have poles as endpoints. We derive the differential equations for arc-length-parametrized loxodromes and introduce coordinates in which they are represented by straight lines. We solve the direct and inverse problems for loxodromic segments on all four surface types and give criteria for maximal loxodromic curves to be geodesics. We show that diffeomorphisms preserving maximal loxodromic curves preserve surface type and that their inverses preserve such curves. These maps preserve maximal meridians and parallels on surfaces with poles, but need not do so on pole-free surfaces. We characterize azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms and, for cylinder-like surfaces, establish criteria for conformality and isometry. In particular, azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms are conformal when both surfaces have poles.

papers.title: Morse index, nullity and Jacobi fields of homogeneous minimal two-spheres in complex hyperquadrics
papers.abstract: We determine the Morse index and normal nullity of all linearly full homogeneous minimal two-spheres in complex hyperquadrics. These invariants satisfy a common relation involving only the ambient dimension and the induced Gauss curvature. We also prove that every normal Jacobi field is integrable through minimal immersions.

papers.title: A constructive computer-assisted existence proof for a Calabi--Yau metric
papers.abstract: We give a rigorous, constructive proof that there exists a Ricci-flat K\"ahler metric on the Fermat quartic hypersurface, independently of Yau's famous theorem, along with an explicit and accurate analytic approximation to the metric. The proof combines numerical techniques to obtain the approximately Ricci flat metric, a fixed point theorem to prove existence, and verified numerics to get the bounds used by the fixed point theorem. The method is general and we discuss the computational issues in applying it to other manifolds.

papers.title: Weak stability of Ricci flow with almost WPIC1 curvature
papers.abstract: We prove weak $L^\infty$ stability for complete, non-collapsed Ricci flows with almost WPIC1 curvature and scaling-invariant curvature bounds. Small $L^\infty$ perturbations of the initial metric admit Ricci-DeTurck flows which remain uniformly close to the background flow and depend Lipschitz continuously on the initial data. This extends an earlier stability theorem of the first and third authors with Lai.

papers.title: Complex singularities and obstructions to pseudo-Einstein structures: An expository note
papers.abstract: This note explains the counterexamples to Lee's conjecture on pseudo-Einstein structures obtained in joint work with Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, and Shuya Matsumoto. The examples are links of normal isolated singularities and occur in every odd real dimension at least three. Each link has vanishing first Betti number and vanishing integral first Chern class of its CR structure, yet admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. We explain how finite first homology relates the existence problem on the link to the canonical divisor at the singular point. For the higher-dimensional examples, we describe the key obstruction directly in terms of the first normal derivatives of the transition functions of a line bundle along an exceptional hypersurface.

papers.title: On real-analytic non-degeneracy of left-symmetric algebras in dimension 3
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that any three-dimensional differentially non-degenerate left-symmetric algebra over $\mathbb R$ is non-degenerate both in the formal and real-analytic categories via the correspondence with Nijenhuis operators.

papers.title: Non-existence of closed embedded magnetic geodesics
papers.abstract: We give a counterexample to S. Novikov's 1982 conjecture that every Riemannian $2$-sphere contains a closed embedded curve of curvature $c$ for every $c>0$.

papers.title: Non self-similar solutions to the Ricci flow coming out of metric cones
papers.abstract: Given an asymptotically conical unstable expanding gradient Ricci soliton, we provide the existence of a family of Ricci flows starting at the same metric cone up to isometry. Moreover, the family of solutions we construct is shown to be parametrized by positive modes of the weighted Lichnerowicz operator associated to the background expanding gradient Ricci soliton. Each solution of this family is shown not to be induced by an expanding gradient Ricci soliton. If the background expander has no non-trivial infinitesimal deformations, we show furthermore that the solutions we provide are not self-similar. We finally prove that solutions are distinct up to isometries preserving the potential function of the background expanding gradient Ricci soliton.

papers.title: Hinge comparison and excess estimates via modified Hessian bounds on manifolds with density
papers.abstract: We study geometric consequences of modified Hessian estimates on Riemannian manifolds with density. For general radial functions, we derive tensorial, spectral, and trace identities for the modified Hessian in the original metric. We also establish a comparison identity relating the modified Hessians of two radial functions and characterize when they are proportional. We then prove a hinge comparison theorem under an upper bound on the modified Hessian, yielding a weighted law of cosines and lower bounds for the excess function. Finally, under nonnegative weighted sectional curvature and suitable density control assumptions, we obtain an Abresch-Gromoll-type upper excess estimate.

papers.title: Spinorial geometry of Bismut--Hermitian--Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract: We present a pair of spinorial equations, generalizing the internal Killing spinor equations of Type I supergravity, and show that they characterize several classes of Bismut-Hermitian-Einstein structures on six-dimensional Riemannian spin manifolds. We show that in this framework the local reduction to a four-dimensional transverse Hermitian geometry is provided by two canonical, commuting, Bismut-parallel Killing vector fields arising as bilinears in the Killing spinors, without assuming compactness. In one class, the transverse geometry is conformally Kahler and both compact and non-compact solutions exist. We also discuss variants that do not admit compact solutions, one of which has hyper-Hermitian transverse geometry. We discuss the relation of these structures to the Hull-Strominger system with closed three-form and to five-dimensional Gauntlett-Kim geometries and provide explicit embeddings in Type I, Type IIB and massive Type IIA supergravity, as well as in generalized supergravity. We illustrate our results with a number of examples, both compact and non-compact.

papers.title: Stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions seven and eight
papers.abstract: We establish optimal sheet separation estimates for stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions up to seven, using an iteration argument in the nonlocal approximation theory of Chan-Dipierro-Serra-Valdinoci. These estimates imply that every stable $s$-minimal hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a hyperplane when $s$ is close to $1$. More generally, every finite Morse index $s$-minimal set in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a half-space. We also establish a compactness theorem for stable $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$. We prove uniform curvature and area estimates for their links and show that, as $s \uparrow 1$, they subconverge graphically in $C^{2,\alpha}$, either with multiplicity one to a classical stable minimal cone, or with multiplicity two to a hyperplane. The stability of Lawson and axisymmetric $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$ shows that these results are optimal.

papers.title: Stability for the Bray-Brendle-Neves Scalar Sphere Rigidity Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $(M^3,g)$ be a closed and oriented 3-dimensional Riemannian manifold with $\pi_2(M)\neq 0$ and let $A_{\pi_2}(M,g)$ denote the least area among homotopically nontrivial two-spheres in $M$. By a theorem of Bray-Brendle-Neves, $A_{\pi_2}(M,g)\inf_M R_g \leq 8\pi$ with equality characterizing the cylindrical geometry $S^2\times\mathbb{R}$. Motivated by Sormani's questions on volume preserving intrinsic flat stability for scalar curvature rigidity problems, we study the almost equality regime of this theorem. We build, using Sweeney's tunnel construction, a sequence satisfying $A_{\pi_2}(M_j,g_j)\inf_{M_j} R_{g_j} \rightarrow 8\pi$ with uniformly bounded volume and diameter whose volume preserving intrinsic flat limit is not the Bray-Brendle-Neves rigidity space, showing that stability fails in general. We then prove stability in two special cases: for sequences of rotationally symmetric metrics (with non-collapsing assumptions) and for sequences of manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature.

papers.title: Nonrigidity of smooth tight surfaces
papers.abstract: We construct smooth isometric embeddings of closed surfaces of positive genus in Euclidean 3-space which are tight, i.e., have minimal total positive curvature, but are not congruent. These embeddings agree outside a compact subset of the region of negative curvature, and enclose different volumes. Thus the rigidity theorem of Alexandrov for analytic tight surfaces does not hold in the smooth category, which settles problems of Nirenberg and Banchoff-Kuhnel.

papers.title: The Cauchy problem for skew-torsion-parallel spinors with applications to supergravity
papers.abstract: We solve the Cauchy problem for an irreducible real spinor parallel with respect to a metric connection with skew-symmetric torsion on a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, proving that it is well-posed modulo an obstruction that we identify explicitly, and obtaining an initial-data characterization of such spinors. Our proof relies on the theory of spinorial forms, which we use to explicitly integrate the coupled flow for the spinor and underlying metric via a rotated pull-back action of the flow generated by a vector field on the Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma$. We characterize the corresponding constraint equations as an explicit exterior differential system and describe all its solutions in terms of contact structures and flat foliations, obtaining a complete classification in the compact case. In particular, we conclude that every oriented compact three-manifold arises as the Cauchy hypersurface of a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold equipped with a skew-torsion parallel spinor. Building on these results, we study the interaction between the four-dimensional Neveu-Schwarz supergravity evolution flow on an abelian bundle gerbe and the spinorial evolution flow determined by its supersymmetric conditions, which we prove to be well-posed and compatible. This establishes the well-posedness of the supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz system in four dimensions and provides an initial-data characterization of supersymmetry. Furthermore, we obtain a strong rigidity result stating that every globally hyperbolic supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz solution with a compact Cauchy hypersurface is flat and has vanishing bundle-gerbe curvature.

papers.title: A transition calculus for 0-pseudodifferential operators with applications to gas giant geometry
papers.abstract: A gas giant Riemannian metric $g$ on a compact $n$-dimensional manifold-with-boundary $M$ blows up at the boundary $\partial M$ at the rate $1/x^\alpha$, for $\alpha \in (0,2)$, where $x \in C^\infty(M)$ is a boundary-defining function. Such metrics arise in the modeling of acoustic waves in gaseous planets. De Hoop-Ilmavirta-Kykk\"{a}nen-Mazzeo [arXiv:2403.05475] showed that, if $\alpha > 2/n$, the Laplace-Beltrami operator $\Delta_g$ is essentially self-adjoint and has discrete spectrum. Moreover, its spectrum is stable under truncations of $M$. The proof leverages the 0-calculus of Mazzeo-Melrose. We extend this theory by introducing a 0-transition calculus for studying families of 0-operators. We demonstrate a parametrix construction for $\Delta_g$ that is stable under truncations. Using this, we study the behavior of the resolvent of $\Delta_g$ under truncation and extend the characterization of the spectrum obtained by de Hoop-Ilmavirta-Kykk\"{a}nen-Mazzeo. In particular, we prove that (on appropriate functional-analytic domains) simple eigenvalues admit asymptotic expansions in the truncation parameter $\epsilon$ and that the corresponding eigenfunctions admit joint asymptotic expansions in $(\epsilon, x)$.

papers.title: Euclidean filling inequalities in CAT(0) spaces
papers.abstract: We clarify and streamline OpenAI's proof of the sharp Euclidean filling inequalities in CAT(0) spaces. We extend the result to complete spaces without assuming properness or compact support, and we establish rigidity in the equality case.

papers.title: The Isoperimetric Flow and Synthetic Scalar Curvature for Causal Variational Principles
papers.abstract: An isoperimetric flow is introduced in the setting of causal variational principles. Describing the whole space by the support of a minimizing measure, we define an area functional on subsets by a surface layer integral. Mean curvature is defined via the first variation of this area functional. Using the method of minimizing movement, the isoperimetric flow is constructed as a Lipschitz curve of measures with prescribed volume change. As illustrating examples, we introduce and analyze ``smeared variants'' of the mean curvature flow in Euclidean space and on a Riemannian manifold. In these examples, it is shown that our area functional coincides with the usual area up to specified curvature corrections. As an application of our general results, by analyzing the volume and area of small isoperimetric balls, we introduce notions of local dimension and synthetic scalar curvature.

papers.title: Making Poisson {\sigma} again - an étude on groupoidal gauging, anomalies, gerbes, and defects
papers.abstract: The Poisson $\sigma$-model (PSM) over a closed worldsheet $\Sigma$ is reinterpreted as a theory of connections on a trivial principaloid bundle $P_0 = \Sigma \times G \to \Sigma$ with the symplectic structure groupoid $(G,\omega)$ integrating the Poisson target $(M,\Pi)$, and that of sections of the shadow bundle $F_0 = \Sigma \times M \to \Sigma$ - as defined in 2503.09886 [math.DG]. The flat directions of the PSM are explained as linearisations of automorphisms of $P_0$, modelled on maps from $\Sigma$ into the group of lagrangean bisections of $G$, which induce Poisson automorphisms of $(M,\Pi)$. The gauge anomaly of the ensuing field theory is derived and demonstrated to vanish for prequantisable $\omega$. A general anomaly-cancellation mechanism is proposed, which couples the bare model - rewritten as the holonomy of a connection-dependent trivial gerbe on $F_0$ - to a background gerbe over $M$ endowed with a $G$-equivariant structure. The coupling takes the form of the tensor product of the two gerbes and the extended PSM is defined as the holonomy of the product gerbe. An essential generalisation of the theory is then proposed - to shadows $F$ of principaloid bundles $P$ of arbitrary topology, in keeping with the interpretation of the gauging as descent to the orbistack $M//G$. The generalisation uses local product gerbes depending on local connections over trivialisations of $F$. The $G$-equivariant structure is proven to ensure a 2-stacky descent of the local gerbes to a global one over $F$. Its holonomy is taken as the definition of the generalised PSM. A cohomological discussion of obstructions against the descent is provided. Finally, a reformulation of the generalised PSM as a field theory with a topological gauge-symmetry defect is given, in which the $G$-equivariant structure is employed - alongside the transition cocycle of $P$ - as the datum of the defect.

papers.title: On the atomic decomposition of complete intersections in toric varieties
papers.abstract: Building on Liu's and Liu--Sheshmani's systematized description of Kontsevich's localization methods in toric varieties, we develop a computational framework for genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants of smooth projective toric varieties and their smooth complete intersections. This is grounded in equivariant localization and the combinatorial structure of toric fans. We describe how the geometric data required by the localization formulas can be recovered directly from the fan and extend the existing software for flag varieties to compute the small quantum multiplication by the first Chern class. The implementation also incorporates cyclic determinants and regularized-exponent multisets, providing computational tools for investigating the atomic decomposition of quantum cohomology. Using this framework, we obtain the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^5$. Also applying new methods to study Hodge atoms in Fano fivefolds, we recover the nonrationality of every smooth complete intersection of a quadric and a cubic in $\mathbb{P}^7$, due to Cavenaghi--Katzarkov--Kontsevich, and we prove the nonrationality of every smooth quartic double fivefold and every smooth quartic fivefold.

papers.title: Generalized Kosmann derivative and symmetry operators on Dirac structures
papers.abstract: We develop a spinorial symmetry framework for metric Dirac structures in $H$-twisted exact Courant algebroids. A generalized metric equips a Dirac structure with an intrinsic Riemannian Lie-algebroid geometry and identifies it isometrically with the positive subbundle of the generalized tangent bundle. For sections preserving the generalized metric, we prove an exact intertwining between the positive-spinor Kosmann--Dorfman action and the intrinsic Kosmann derivative. The comparison is independent of the auxiliary compatible generalized connection. Within the intrinsic geometry we derive Killing--Yano (KY) and conformal Killing--Yano (CKY) integrability identities, construct Killing-spinor-preserving operators from odd special KY and even special closed CKY forms, and obtain these forms from Hermitian bilinears of Killing spinors with imaginary Killing number. We illustrate the framework on a global Dirac structure over $S^2\times S^1$ with nontrivial $H$-flux class and rank-two anchor. Its spin connection and symmetry operators are explicit, and its Killing-spinor space is a transverse family $C^\infty(S^1,\mathbb C^2)$. Finally, intrinsic Killing sections act on Killing spinors by a Lie algebra representation. For a graph Dirac structure over $S^3$, the odd Jacobi identity of the Hermitian-current bracket fails by a phase, and adjoining a single even phase generator yields a Lie superalgebra. These results connect generalized isometries, hidden spinorial symmetries, and flux-sensitive Lie-algebroid geometry.

papers.title: The Bolza Surface Does Not Locally Minimize the Diameter Function
papers.abstract: We study the diameter function on the Teichm\"uller space of closed hyperbolic Riemann surfaces. Although the Bolza surface maximizes the systole among hyperbolic surfaces of genus 2, its extremal behavior with respect to the diameter function is less clear. Using first variations of distances at diameter pairs and linear programming duality, we establish a sufficient criterion for a surface not to be a local minimizer of the diameter function. More precisely, we show that if each diameter pair can be assigned a simple closed geodesic formed by two minimizing geodesic segments joining its endpoints, with distinct assigned geodesics pairwise disjoint, then a deformation varying only the length parameters in Fenchel-Nielsen coordinates strictly decreases the diameter. The assigned geodesics extend to a pants decomposition, and the decrease is detected by a strictly negative upper bound for the first-order variation of the diameter. We then apply this criterion to the Bolza surface and prove that it is not a local minimizer of the diameter function on the Teichm\"uller space of genus 2.

papers.title: Renormalized volume, Generalized Loewner energy, and Grunsky determinant of multiply connected domains
papers.abstract: We define and study three M\"obius invariant functionals for multiply connected planar domains with finitely many boundary components: the Loewner energy, the renormalized volume, and the Grunsky determinant. Using quasiconformal variations, we prove that when the boundary curves are sufficiently regular, the three functionals differ only by a modulus-dependent constant. We also prove that the Loewner energy is finite if and only if every boundary curve is a Weil--Petersson quasicircle. Moreover, we prove that the three functionals all attain their unique extremal value at the circle domains. In particular, the Loewner energy is zero if and only if it is evaluated at a circle domain. Finally, we use the minimization of Loewner energy to give a new proof of the finitely connected version of Koebe uniformization theorem.

papers.title: Chern characteristic classes of normal bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds in generalized flag manifolds
papers.abstract: We study Chern characteristic classes of normal vector bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ in complex generalized flag manifolds $G_n/P_n$. This procedure can be regarded as the relative version of Schubert calculus for the pair $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ and $G_n/P_n$. The CW structure and additive structure of the cohomology of $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$ allows inductive calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$. The combination of representation theory and algebraic geometry allows to derive analogous properties for the isotropic Grassmannians $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$ via their embeddings in $\mathrm{Gr}(m, k)$. Then the induced CW structure yields the additive structure on the cohomology of $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$, and consequently leads to the calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$.

papers.title: The uniqueness of smooth stationary black holes
papers.abstract: We show that the domain of outer communications of a smooth, asymptotically flat, stationary vacuum spacetime describing a single rotating non-degenerate black hole is isometric to the domain of outer communications of a subextremal Kerr solution under reasonable geometric and physical assumptions, without analyticity or any smallness assumptions. The method is to apply Harrison transform to construct a family of solutions of Einstein--Maxwell equations. Combining null area comparison with the area-charge inequality, we show that, in the limiting transformed geometry, the bifurcate sphere has area radius one and constant electric and magnetic flux densities, with the original ADM mass normalized to $M=1$. These identities imply the technical assumptions of Ionescu--Klainerman, yielding the identification with Kerr.
